analysis: The batch is documentation-only. docs/README.md (head lines 3-8, 34) updates the date, drops the "retained console snapshot" wording, and relabels the console link. docs/architecture/README.md (head line 10) relabels the same link. docs/architecture/components/console-ui.md goes from about 338 lines to a 10-line pointer saying the console now lives in the platform repo (the pinned platform link is retained) and that this repo keeps no console source, build, test, CI or git hooks. No executable code, provider keys, attestation, WebSocket contract, encryption or cache-storage behavior (A-001, A-003, A-010, A-015/A-016, T-041, TB-002/003/007/009/011/012) changes. Removing the console-ui documentation drops descriptions of console behavior: the same-origin /api proxy, Privy token and API-key handling, the sealed-chat path, CSP and mock-auth caveats. Those belong to the backend and console scope the canonical threat model already marks out of scope, and they now live in the platform repo. The patch only documents the removal, so it creates no provider-side security regression. Unverified: the snapshot removal in #1625 and the platform repo's console are outside the supplied evidence. Dangling doc links may remain elsewhere, for example reference/configuration.md, developer/build.md, developer/test.md and encryption.md, which the old page cited. These are documentation hygiene issues, not security ones. The threat-model YAML still references no console files in the supplied definitions. Nothing in the evidence invalidates a threat-model assumption.
